description.value: Ronning's Garden is a heritage garden carved from BC's northern rainforest by Norwegian homesteader Bernt Ronning, who established his homestead here in 1910 near the terminus of the old San Josef Wagon Road and filled it with exotic plants ordered from around the world. The garden is renowned for hosting one of the oldest and largest Monkey Puzzle trees in British Columbia. Maintained today by a small group of volunteers and free to enter, it is a remarkable off-the-beaten-path destination for cyclists exploring the Cape Scott region of Vancouver Island North, reached by a ten-minute walk along a restored section of the historic wagon road.

address.value: San Josef Main Fsr, Holberg, British Columbia, Canada

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A genuinely notable heritage attraction — one of the oldest/largest Monkey Puzzle trees in BC, free admission, volunteer-operated — that would appeal to cyclists doing the Cape Scott / northern Vancouver Island circuit; the absence of confirmed cycling amenities is expected for a remote garden of this type and does not disqualify it as an Attraction listing.
enrichment_extras.notes: Contact for donations/e-transfer: ronningsgarden@gmail.com (from website). Access: from Port Hardy follow signs to Holberg, then San Josef Main towards Cape Scott Provincial Park; garden turnoff is between km markers 14 and 15.

wow_evidence: Century-old homestead garden of exotic plantings in the northern rainforest, famed for giant monkey puzzle trees; beloved north-island oddity.
